title: Storm in Bay of Bengal forecast to hit Andhra coast between Nellore and Tuni on Friday
dek: The IMD expects the system, to be named Akvan, to cross the coast around noon on 20 November as a very severe cyclonic storm with winds of up to 145 kmph, and warns of a storm surge of up to 1.5 metres.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The weather system over the south Bay of Bengal is forecast to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Nellore and Tuni around noon on Friday, 20 November, as a very severe cyclonic storm with sustained winds of 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said on Monday, giving a landfall forecast for the first time. It warned of a storm surge of 1 to 1.5 metres above the normal tide that could flood low-lying areas of six coastal districts.

In its national bulletin issued at 4 pm IST, the IMD said the deep depression was expected to strengthen into a cyclonic storm on Monday evening, when it will be named Akvan, and into a severe cyclonic storm by Tuesday evening. It kept a pre-cyclone watch for Andhra Pradesh and the adjoining south Odisha coast, and forecast heavy rain over coastal Andhra Pradesh, north Tamil Nadu, Odisha and Telangana later in the week, with heavy rain at isolated places in Gangetic West Bengal on 19 and 20 November.

## What happened

At 11.30 am IST on Monday the deep depression lay near latitude 11.7°N and longitude 86.0°E, about 650 km east-southeast of Chennai, 730 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam, 850 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha and 620 km northeast of Trincomalee in Sri Lanka, the bulletin said. It had moved north-northwestwards at 17 kmph over the previous six hours, more than twice as fast as overnight, with winds of 50-60 kmph gusting to 70 kmph.

The IMD's forecast table shows the storm strengthening more slowly than in its 2.30 am bulletin but heading further south. Winds are expected to reach 90-100 kmph by 11.30 am on Tuesday, when it becomes a severe cyclonic storm, and 105-115 kmph by Thursday morning. It is forecast to become a very severe cyclonic storm late on Thursday night and to be near 15.8°N, 81.0°E, just off the central Andhra Pradesh coast, at 11.30 am on Friday, with winds of 120-130 kmph. After crossing the coast it is expected to weaken to a severe cyclonic storm by Friday night as it moves inland.

Satellite data showed intense to very intense convection to the west and northwest of the centre, the department's tropical weather outlook said, and conditions including warm seas and an active phase of the Madden-Julian Oscillation, a pulse of cloud and rain that moves around the tropics, favoured further strengthening.

## Storm surge and wind

The bulletin said a storm surge of 1.0 to 1.5 metres was very likely to inundate low-lying areas of Prakasam, Bapatla, Krishna, West Godavari, Konaseema and Kakinada districts at the time of landfall, with the highest surge expected over Bapatla, Krishna and West Godavari.

Along and off the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts, it forecast squally winds of 40-50 kmph gusting to 60 kmph until Tuesday, gale-force winds of 60-70 kmph gusting to 80 kmph until Thursday morning, and 120-130 kmph gusting to 145 kmph from Thursday night until noon on Friday, with "phenomenal" seas and waves of 9 to 14 metres. It warned of major damage to thatched and kutcha houses, power and communication poles, standing crops, banana and papaya plantations and coconut trees, flooding of roads and escape routes, and disruption of rail traffic and overhead power lines, and advised that people in coastal huts be moved to safer places.

## Where rain is forecast

The rainfall warnings in the 4 pm bulletin, by the IMD's dates:

- Coastal Andhra Pradesh: heavy rain at isolated places on 18 November, then heavy to very heavy rain at a few places with isolated extremely heavy falls (21 cm or more) on 19 and 20 November.
- North Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal: heavy rain at isolated places on 17 and 20 November, and heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 18 and 19 November.
- Odisha: heavy rain at isolated places on 18 November, and heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places from 19 to 21 November.
- Eastern Telangana: heavy to very heavy rain at isolated places on 20 November.
- Gangetic West Bengal: light to moderate rain at many places, with heavy rain at isolated places, on 19 and 20 November.
- Rayalaseema, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Vidarbha and east Madhya Pradesh: heavy rain at isolated places between 19 and 21 November.

## Warnings for fishermen and preparations

Fishermen have been told not to go into the southwest Bay of Bengal until 19 November, the central Bay of Bengal until 20 November, the Andaman Sea until 17 November and the northwest Bay of Bengal, the waters off Odisha and West Bengal, on 19 and 20 November. In Andhra Pradesh, fishermen have been told not to go to sea until 20 November, according to reports. Odisha has alerted all 30 of its districts, opened round-the-clock control rooms and put teams of the National Disaster Response Force, its own disaster response force and fire services on standby, reports said.

## Background

Akvan would be the third cyclone to threaten the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts since late October. Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast in late October, and its remnants caused floods and a landslide in southern Odisha that killed at least three people in Kandhamal district. Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu crossed the coast near Ongole on 3 November, damaging crops on more than 30,000 hectares in 15 districts of Andhra Pradesh, according to the state government, though no deaths were reported.

November is one of the most active months for cyclones in the Bay of Bengal, after the south-west monsoon withdraws. The names used in the north Indian Ocean are drawn in sequence from a list contributed by 13 countries in the region; Arnab was proposed by Bangladesh, Murasu by India and Akvan by Iran, according to the published list.

For Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, a third storm in a month would arrive on soil that is already wet and over kharif crops, including paddy, that are close to harvest. Exact effects will depend on where the storm crosses the coast. The IMD's earliest outlooks pointed further north, towards the stretch between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur; its latest bulletin has moved the expected crossing south, to central and south coastal Andhra Pradesh.

## What happens next

If the storm follows the forecast track, the department is expected to move from a pre-cyclone watch to a cyclone alert and then a cyclone warning for the stretch of coast where landfall is expected, the third and fourth stages of its warning system. The landfall point may still shift; weather models differ on the storm's later movement and strength, according to reports citing the IMD's outlook.

## Key numbers

- 650 km: distance from Chennai at 11.30 am IST on Monday
- 730 km: distance from Visakhapatnam
- Around noon, 20 November: forecast landfall between Nellore and Tuni
- 120-130 kmph, gusting to 145 kmph: forecast winds at landfall
- 1-1.5 metres: forecast storm surge in six Andhra Pradesh districts
- 21 cm or more: extremely heavy rain forecast at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh on 19-20 November
